papers.title: Influence of sub/super- <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" altimg="si64.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1561"> <mml:mi>β</mml:mi> </mml:math> transus HIP treatments on the fatigue crack initiation of PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V produced with varying defect content
papers.abstract: Hot isostatic pressing (HIP) is commonly applied to additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V to eliminate lack-of-fusion (LoF) defects; however, significant differences in fatigue performance are often observed even when residual porosity is comparable. This study investigates whether fatigue behaviour in PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V material with varying defect content is controlled by process defects or by microstructure-dependent crack initiation mechanisms. Specimens were produced using two process themes, a minimal porosity (MP) and a high productivity (HP) condition with reduced volumetric energy input, and subsequently HIP treated below or above the β -transus temperature. X-ray computed tomography confirmed that HIP effectively healed LoF defects in the HP material, reducing residual porosity to levels comparable to MP builds. Fatigue testing revealed that, once defects were eliminated, fatigue life depended strongly on the HIP microstructure: sub- β HIP consistently produced longer lives than super- β HIP across all stress levels. EBSD analysis showed that sub- β HIP generated a fine α structure that distributed cyclic plasticity across many grains, whereas super- β HIP formed large prior- β grains containing coarse α colonies with very fine lamellar structure within each colony. These colonies acted as microstructural units, concentrating cyclic slip into long bands and promoting early crack initiation. The results show that HIP reduces defect density and the remaining fatigue failures are predominantly governed by microstructural mechanisms. After excluding a few samples with defect initiated failures, fatigue life was controlled by colony slip localisation, identifying the α colony size as the dominant microstructural fatigue length scale. Tailoring HIP temperature provides a route to achieving wrought-comparable fatigue performance in high-productivity PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V. • Fatigue tests on PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V ELI show processing and structure control life. • Sub- β HIP improves fatigue by finer, intertwined α that delays cracks. • HIP healed high productivity builds match wrought fatigue, validating fast PBF-LB. • Recrystallised equiaxed α grains show level stress dependent activity affecting fatigue life.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究了热等静压（HIP）处理温度对增材制造Ti-6Al-4V疲劳性能的影响，完全符合后处理控制方向。
llm.why_not_core: Only considers HIP, not other post-processes like machining or peening; however, this is a core study within the HIP sub-topic.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究HIP温度（亚/超β相变点）对消除缺陷后疲劳寿命的控制机制
summary_zh.method: 制备两种缺陷水平的PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V，分别进行亚β和超β HIP处理，进行疲劳测试和微观表征
summary_zh.result: 亚β HIP的细α结构延长疲劳寿命，超β HIP的粗α团簇促进裂纹萌生
summary_zh.validation: 通过疲劳试验、CT和EBSD验证缺陷消除和微观结构影响

summary_en.motivation: To investigate whether HIP temperature (sub/super β transus) governs fatigue life after defect closure in PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Two sets of PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V specimens with different initial defect levels were HIP treated below or above the β transus, then subjected to fatigue testing and microstructural characterization.
summary_en.result: Sub-β HIP produced a fine α structure that improved fatigue life, while super-β HIP formed coarse α colonies that localized cyclic slip and promoted early crack initiation.
summary_en.validation: Fatigue tests, X-ray computed tomography for porosity, and EBSD for crystallographic orientation validated the microstructural effects.
